fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Walkway; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Limited Visibility; Single Access Point; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear a turning or staging area within the driveway or parking area so emergency vehicles can reposition without backing onto the road.
• Cut back dense vegetation that limits visibility of the main residence from the driveway approach.
• Trim shrubs or branches growing close to the detached structure to keep them from blocking access around it.
• Mark or clearly identify any walking path connecting the main residence to the detached structure so responders can navigate between buildings quickly.
• Keep the walkway clear of overgrown vegetation so responders can move between structures on foot without obstruction.
• Because there is only one vehicle access point, keep the driveway free of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris that could block an emergency vehicle from reaching the residence.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Large Trees; Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Limited Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Vegetation Along Driveway; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin trees on all sides of the house to create open space between the canopy and the structure.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees near the house so flames cannot climb from the ground into the tree tops.
• Thin trees within the two visible clusters to break up the concentration of vegetation near the structure.
• Cut or mow grass around the house regularly, especially during dry periods, to keep it short.
• Clear shrubs scattered near the house, prioritizing those closest to walls, vents, and corners.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles, including emergency equipment, can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove shrubs and low branches growing along the driveway edges that could carry fire toward the house.
• Keep the open green space adjacent to the structure mowed and free of dead or dry plant material.
• Maintain clear sight lines and open ground around all sides of the house so firefighters can move and work freely.
• Verify that both access routes are free of obstructions, overhanging vegetation, and debris so emergency vehicles can enter and exit without difficulty.
